# Bike recalls, read like surveillance data. [Which parts fail, which hazards follow, and what is changing.]{.accent}

Every bicycle, e-bike, and component recall published by the US Consumer Product Safety Commission and Health Canada, sorted with a written case definition, classified by the part that failed and the hazard it caused, and checked against hand-labelled records.

[Open the dashboard](dashboard.qmd){.btn .btn-accent} [Key findings](#key-findings){.btn .btn-ghost} [Code on GitHub](https://github.com/emmabranch/bike-recall-surveillance){.btn .btn-ghost}

## What this is

Recalls are a regulator's response to a safety problem, so a collection of them can be read the way an epidemiologist reads disease notifications. This project applies that approach to bicycles:

- **A case definition.** Written rules decide which recalls count (bicycles, e-bikes, components, and accessories) and which do not (helmets, exercise bikes, scooters, and motorbikes), with every decision recorded.
- **Classification.** Each recall is coded by what was recalled, the part that failed, and the hazard it caused.
- **Validation.** The rules were checked against 100 hand-labelled records, with a further 40 held back as an independent test.
- **Caveats.** Recalls are passively reported and negotiated, and regulations have changed over time. Those limits shape what these numbers can and cannot say.

The analysis is industry-wide. It does not rank or compare companies. Brand names appear only as published in the official notices, and you can search for them on the dashboard.

## Key findings {#key-findings}

```{r findings}
#| output: asis
cat(sprintf('<div class="finding-grid">
<div class="finding"><h3>Falls dominate</h3><p>%s of recall events involve a fall or crash hazard. Fire, laceration, and chemical hazards together make up the rest.</p></div>
<div class="finding"><h3>Forks fail most often</h3><p>%s of events trace back to the %s, ahead of stems and handlebars, wheels and hubs, and frames.</p></div>
<div class="finding"><h3>E-bike recalls are rising</h3><p>There were %s e-bike recall events in %s to %s, against %s in the three years before. Some of that may reflect growth in e-bike sales, which these data cannot measure.</p></div>
<div class="finding"><h3>E-bikes bring fire</h3><p>%s of e-bike recall events involve a fire or burn hazard, against %s of other bicycle recalls, mostly from batteries and chargers.</p></div>
</div>',
  pct(share_fall),
  pct(share_top_comp), str_to_lower(top_component$failed_component),
  ebike_recent, last_full_year - 2, last_full_year, ebike_before,
  pct(ebike_fire_share), pct(other_fire_share)))
```

::: {.caveat-box}
**Recalls are not injuries.** A recall shows that a regulator and a company acted on a problem, not how many people were hurt. There is no count of bikes sold, so these figures cannot be read as risk. Read the full [surveillance caveats](caveats.qmd) and [methods](methods.qmd).
:::
